# `maximum-decreased`

maximum decreased

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `maximum-decreased` (both directions), `maximum-decreased-in-request`, `maximum-decreased-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`maximum` or `exclusiveMaximum` decreased.

## Why this default

In requests: larger numbers are rejected. In responses: clients receive smaller numbers, which is safe.

## Example

From test case [`maximum-decreased`](../../test/cases/maximum-decreased/): maximum lowered on a request number.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: integer
-           maximum: 100
+           maximum: 50
```

Findings:

- `maximum-decreased-in-request` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  maximum-decreased: info
```

## How to fix

Keep the old maximum in requests.
